title: US Empire WITHDRAWAL Begins as Bonds Break, Bessent Defeated & Trump Escalates BIG
speaker: Sean Foo

macro_themes.view: 10y at 5.34% (25-year high), 30y at 5.7% and the move toward 6% probably not over; Treasury avoiding long-dated issuance.
Energy-driven inflation (diesel ~$6.50, gas >$4.30) is entrenched; consumers stretched, sentiment in the gutter.
S&P dividend yield at a record-low 1.07% (below dot-com peak); stocks are not a safe haven and will be hit when earnings reflect consumer damage.
Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco and fighting spilling to the Red Sea - brace for more energy price shocks; Iran war costs add to bond issuance.
Bessent's forecasts have failed; if Iran outlasts his '2 weeks to collapse' claim, investors may dump more US bonds.

calls.reason: Spending will not stop, inflation entrenched, Treasury credibility falling; bond values could crash further.
calls.quote: if you stay in dollar bonds, values could crash even further, because the spending is not going to stop.

calls.reason: 30-year just hit 5.7% with the move toward 6% likely not finished.
calls.quote: the 30-year just hit 5.7%, and the move towards 6% is probably not over yet.

calls.reason: Conflict spreading from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea with Houthi attacks on Aramco; US refineries at 92.5% leave no buffer.
calls.quote: So, brace for more energy price shocks in the weeks immediately ahead.

calls.condition: If yields keep pushing toward 6%, the real economy and then stocks get hit.
calls.reason: Record-low dividend yield, stretched consumers and rising yields; stocks will be hammered when earnings reflect the damage.
calls.quote: US stocks will also get hammered when earnings eventually reflect the damage to consumer spending.

notes: Livestream; no date spoken, listing approx_date used. Equity bias is 'sooner or later' with no timing; recorded medium/long term bearish. Oil bias inferred from 'energy price shocks' (CL used as proxy; he mostly quotes gasoline/diesel retail prices).
